title: Call handshake envelopes for streaming invocations and legacy fallthrough
creator: Lena García
description: Problem: OpenAI-style tool calling (name + JSON schema) and our legacy function invocation surface (positional/legacy params, different naming conventions, no streaming semantics) both need to remain supported. Current shims address name aliasing but do not define a streaming-first handshake or a typed envelope that preserves provenance, allows schema negotiation, and enables graceful fallthrough to legacy function handlers. Goal: design and implement an invocation handshake envelope (v1) that standardizes metadata for streamed tool/function calls, supports name aliasing and deprecation metadata, and encodes backward-compatible fallthrough behavior so runtime can route to explicit tool implementations or legacy function handlers without ambiguity. Success metrics: 1) No functional regressions for existing customers (automated smoke tests pass), 2) Streaming tool calls can carry metadata and structured result envelopes with <5ms median extra processing latency, 3) 0 critical customer incidents in first month of canary rollout, 4) Clear telemetry showing correct routing and alias resolution for >=99.9% of calls.
acceptance_criteria: Define 'invocation_envelope.v1' spec and publish to design doc
Runtime accepts both wrapped (envelope) and raw legacy invocations and translates deterministically
Streaming frames include explicit 'frame_type' markers: metadata, chunk, tool_event, error, done
Name alias resolution uses ordered name_alias_map with stable deterministic tie-breaker
Backwards fallthrough header 'X-Legacy-Fallthrough' toggles routing to legacy handler and is honored
Full test matrix (OpenAI-style tools + 3 legacy variants) green in CI with canary coverage
implementation_plan: Write protocol spec: invocation_envelope.v1 (fields: invocation_id, client_version, name_candidates, preferred_schema_hash, aliases, provenance, streaming_capabilities)
Add server-side parser in runtime to accept envelope OR legacy payload; produce unified internal Invocation object
Implement streaming frame handler with these frame types: metadata, chunk, tool_event, done, final_envelope
Implement name_alias_map lookup with telemetry tags and TTL-based alias backfills
Add parameter coercion layer: object->positional mapping for known legacy signatures and basic type coercion rules
Create migration harness and test fixtures covering: schema negotiation, streaming re-order, mid-stream errors, legacy fallthrough
Ship canary to 5% of Hosted API traffic, monitor routing and errors, iterate
Document the public API changes and add SDK examples for streaming tool calls using the envelope
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Ambiguous name resolution between similar tool names. Mitigation: deterministic tie-breaker (highest explicit alias priority, then exact match, then historical usage heuristic) and telemetry to detect collisions.
Risk: Increased per-request CPU for envelope parsing. Mitigation: lightweight binary-coded frame headers and cache parsed schemas on hot paths; measure overhead in microbenchmarks.
Risk: Legacy handlers may reject coerced params. Mitigation: add opt-in 'strict_mode' flag in envelope; default to permissive with warnings sent to customer account dashboard.
Risk: Streaming ordering assumptions vary by client. Mitigation: include explicit sequence numbers in chunk frames and make ordering enforcement optional with a best-effort default.

qa_plan: Unit tests for parser, alias map, and parameter coercion (target 100% branch coverage for new modules)
Integration tests: stream a range of tool sizes (small, medium, large), simulate mid-stream error and recovery
End-to-end tests with legacy function handlers enabled: three permutations of payload shapes
Performance regression: benchmark end-to-end latency against baseline for 1k qps synthetic workload
Canary monitoring: error-rate, routing_mismatch_rate, alias_collision_count, p50/p95 extra processing latency
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): merge behind feature flag into main, enable in staging
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 2% Hosted API traffic for 24h, monitor signals
Phase 2 (ramped canary): increase to 10% for one week if stable
Phase 3 (migration window): enable default fallthrough behavior for Dedicated customers with notice; provide SDK helper for migration
Phase 4 (GA): flip feature flag for Hosted API after two weeks of healthy metrics; publish migration guide and changelog
notes: Related internal discussion: prefer envelope over extending existing function surface to reduce ambiguity when streaming and carrying provenance.
We will avoid adding breaking changes to the public tool schema; envelope is an additive wrapper and the runtime will continue supporting raw legacy calls.
Telemetry keys to emit: invocation.envelope.present, invocation.routing.target, invocation.alias.origin, invocation.schema.mismatch
